name: distressor-drum-glue
description: The everyday musical UADx Distressor move on a stereo drum bus: gentle program-dependent glue + 2nd-harmonic warmth that mostly keeps the punch. Ratio 2:1 (the Distressor's silky transparent 'parabolic' soft knee), input 5 for a couple dB of drive/GR, attack 8 (slow = transients punch through), release 5 (medium, breathes), AUDIO = Dist 2 (even-harmonic warmth, ~+9 dB H2 measured at musical settings), DETECTOR = HP so the kick stops triggering GR and stays forward. VALIDATED on the Watercolors warm drum bus: crest 17.17->15.06 (held within ~2.1 dB), LRA 2.44->1.96 (a touch tighter), +2.0 LU denser, true-peak -0.99, low end forward (HP detector lets the kick through). Glue + warmth that keeps the feel. For heavier/forward use distressor-aggressive-drums; for parallel use distressor-parallel-smash. NOTE: every render is peak-normalized to -1 dBFS, so compression shows up as +LU at constant peak and a few dB of crest drop is expected even when gentle.
intended_for: a stereo drum bus / submix that wants Distressor glue + warmth while keeping its transients
plugin_build: uaudio_distressor.vst3 (UADx native build — RENDERS headless & processes offline, verified changed:true; the /Components/UAD Empirical Labs Distressor.component twin passes through offline, do not use it). UADx native is the no-iLok perpetual lineage, but re-verify changed:true on a new machine.
notes: ratio / detector / audio are STRING enums — apply-vst-chain's number-only dict CANNOT set them (you can't pass '4:1'/'HP'/'Dist 2'). This MUST go through apply_vst_preset.py. The four dials (input/attack/release/output/mix) and headroom ARE numeric and could be set via apply-vst-chain, but ratio defines the whole character, so use the harness.

ATTACK dial: 0 = FASTEST (clamps transients, crest collapses ~18->10), 10 = SLOWEST (transients punch through, crest ~18->19). High number = punch. Lower it toward 3-4 for the controlled/aggressive sound.
RELEASE dial: 0 = fast (dense, aggressive, brighter, pumps), 10 = slow (smooth, holds level down). 4 here keeps it breathing without pumping.
INPUT is the drive/threshold: more input = more signal into the detector (more GR) AND harder into the distortion stage (more THD). It colors and compresses together.
DETECTOR HP removes lows from the DETECTOR only (audio low end untouched) so the kick/bass stop pulling GR down — kick punches through and the bus gets louder (rms rose ~+4 dB vs Norm in isolation).
Dist 2 = even/2nd-harmonic warmth (gentle, <1% THD at this drive). For grit use Dist 3 (adds 3rd harmonic). The harness peak-normalizes to -1 dBFS, so A/B at matched loudness before judging.
